$comment: The registry of every validation reason pkinative can return. The reason-parity rule of scripts/verify-docs.ts keeps it in bidirectional sync with the PkiReasonCode union of src/types/pki-reasons.ts and requires a factory for every code in src/core/pki-reasons.ts. A reason is RETURNED in a report, never thrown and never emitted: reason-parity refuses a PKI_REASON_* literal inside a throw, refuses a message beginning with 'pkinative: ' (that prefix marks what is thrown, and keeping it exclusive is what lets a log reader tell an exception from a verdict), and requires the three registries to be disjoint. Unlike PkiErrorCode this vocabulary does NOT freeze at 0.8 — the set of reasons a chain can be rejected grows with the standards — but a removal or a rename is still semver-major.

reasons.returnedWhen: The bytes are not the structure they claim to be.
reasons.remedy: Read the errorCode field: it carries the PkiErrorCode the parser would have thrown, so the reason registry wraps the error registry instead of duplicating it.

reasons.returnedWhen: The validation instant is before the certificate's notBefore.
reasons.remedy: Validate at an instant inside the window, or obtain a certificate that is already valid.

reasons.returnedWhen: The validation instant is after the certificate's notAfter.
reasons.remedy: Renew the certificate. Validating at an earlier instant is only correct when checking a signature made then.

reasons.returnedWhen: No name in the certificate matches the host or address the caller asked about (RFC 6125).
reasons.remedy: A certificate that verifies is not a certificate for the host you connected to. Check the subjectAltName; a matching commonName does not count unless you opted into the deprecated fallback.

reasons.returnedWhen: A certificate on the path carries extKeyUsage and does not name the purpose the caller asked checkExtendedKeyUsage for — or, with requireExplicit, carries no extKeyUsage at all. By default a CA's own extKeyUsage restricts what it may issue for, which no sentence of RFC 5280 requires and every Web PKI validator does.
reasons.remedy: A chain that validates is sound for what its CAs granted, which may not be what you are doing with it. Ask the issuer for a certificate naming the purpose you need; if the restriction comes from a CA above the leaf, that CA was deliberately constrained and the leaf should not have been issued. restrictIssuers: false is the literal-RFC reading, for an internal PKI that puts a purpose on a CA as documentation.

reasons.returnedWhen: A certificate carries a critical extension this implementation does not recognise.
reasons.remedy: RFC 5280 requires refusal, not tolerance: an extension marked critical is one the issuer says must be understood.

reasons.returnedWhen: A name in the certificate falls outside the permitted subtrees a CA above it set.
reasons.remedy: A sub-CA cannot issue for names its issuer withheld. Either the certificate names the wrong host, or it was issued under the wrong CA.

reasons.returnedWhen: A name in the certificate falls inside a subtree a CA above it excluded.
reasons.remedy: An exclusion anywhere on the path wins over every permission; there is no CA below that can grant it back.

reasons.returnedWhen: The certificate is listed in a revocation list that covers it.
reasons.remedy: The message carries the revocation date: a signature made before that instant may still be good, and a caller deciding that needs the date.

reasons.returnedWhen: The revocation list has no nextUpdate, or its nextUpdate has passed beyond the caller staleTolerance.
reasons.remedy: Fetch a current list. An out-of-date list says what was revoked then, not now.

reasons.returnedWhen: The revocation list names a different issuer from the certificate, compared by encoded name.
reasons.remedy: Use the list published by the certificate issuer; a list from another CA says nothing about this certificate.

reasons.returnedWhen: The list was issued by the right CA but its issuingDistributionPoint declares a scope that excludes this certificate — the wrong kind of certificate, or a distribution point the certificate does not name.
reasons.remedy: Fetch the list published at the distribution point the certificate's cRLDistributionPoints names. A list that does not cover a certificate does not list it either, so its silence is not evidence.

reasons.returnedWhen: The list declares onlySomeReasons, so the certificate's absence from it rules out those revocation reasons and no others.
reasons.remedy: Supply the other lists the CA publishes for the remaining reasons. verifyCertificateChain accumulates them (RFC 5280 §6.3.3 reasons_mask) and drops this once the union is complete.

reasons.returnedWhen: No revocation evidence was available: no list, or one whose signature was never checked or did not verify.
reasons.remedy: This is not "not revoked". Proceeding on it is a soft-fail decision to make deliberately, not one a validator should make for you.

reasons.returnedWhen: A revocation answer is about a different certificate, or does not echo the nonce that was sent.
reasons.remedy: Retrying will not help: this response was not produced for this question. Suspect a confused responder, a cache serving another answer, or substitution.

reasons.returnedWhen: No certificate policy survives the whole path, and an explicit policy was required by a CA in it or by the caller.
reasons.remedy: This is the only condition under which policy processing rejects a path. An empty policy tree with nobody requiring an explicit policy is not a failure — the question was never asked.

reasons.returnedWhen: A policyMappings extension names anyPolicy as an issuerDomainPolicy or a subjectDomainPolicy.
reasons.remedy: RFC 5280 forbids it. The mapping is ignored rather than honoured, so the path may still fail for want of a policy.

reasons.returnedWhen: No supplied certificate has a subject equal to this certificate's issuer.
reasons.remedy: Supply the intermediate certificates. A server that sends only its leaf is the usual cause.

reasons.returnedWhen: The issuer's public key does not verify the certificate's signature.
reasons.remedy: A verdict, not an incident: these bytes were not signed by that key.

reasons.returnedWhen: The signature could not be checked here — no Web Crypto, or an algorithm this runtime refuses.
reasons.remedy: This says nothing about whether the signature is valid. Ask again on a runtime that implements the algorithm; never treat it as a rejection.

reasons.returnedWhen: The chain does not end at any supplied trust anchor.
reasons.remedy: Supply the root. A signature that verifies is not a certificate that is trusted.

reasons.returnedWhen: A certificate issued another without asserting cA in basicConstraints, or keyCertSign in keyUsage.
reasons.remedy: Only a CA certificate may issue. This is the check whose absence caused the 2008 Basic Constraints attacks.

reasons.returnedWhen: A pathLenConstraint in the chain, or the caller's own bound, is exceeded.
reasons.remedy: Shorten the chain, or use a CA whose constraint permits it.

reasons.returnedWhen: The same certificate appears twice in the chain.
reasons.remedy: Remove the duplicate. A path that revisits a certificate is not a path.

reasons.returnedWhen: The SignedData has no SignerInfo. RFC 5652 allows it — it is how .p7b certificate bundles ship a chain — but it signs nothing.
reasons.remedy: This is a certificate bundle, not a signature. Read its certificates with parseSignedData; there is nothing to verify.

reasons.returnedWhen: No certificate carried in the message or supplied by the caller matches the signer's identifier — by issuer DER and serial, or by subjectKeyIdentifier extension.
reasons.remedy: Supply the signer's certificate through the certificates option. The identifier is not signed, so it only selects candidates; the signature decides between them.

reasons.returnedWhen: The content is detached (eContent absent) and neither the content nor its digest was supplied.
reasons.remedy: Pass content, or contentDigest when the signer used signed attributes. Absent content is never treated as empty content.

reasons.returnedWhen: The content does not hash, under the signer's digestAlgorithm, to the value of its messageDigest attribute.
reasons.remedy: The content was altered, or it is not the content that was signed. For a PDF, check that the digest covers exactly the /ByteRange; for S/MIME, that the MIME entity was canonicalised to CRLF.

reasons.returnedWhen: A signed attribute breaks the rules of RFC 5652 §11 or RFC 5035: contentType or messageDigest missing, repeated or multi-valued; contentType different from eContentType; an attribute that may only be signed found among the unsigned ones; or signed attributes absent where the content type requires them.
reasons.remedy: The signer's software is non-conforming, or the attributes were tampered with. The message names the rule broken.

reasons.returnedWhen: The digest named by digestAlgorithm, the one built into signatureAlgorithm and the one in a CMSAlgorithmProtection attribute disagree; or the signer used an algorithm refused outright, such as MD5 or id-ecPublicKey in place of an ECDSA signature algorithm.
reasons.remedy: Treat the signature as unverifiable. Disagreement between these fields is the shape of an algorithm-substitution attack (RFC 6211), and no conforming signer produces it.

reasons.returnedWhen: The signer's signingCertificate or signingCertificateV2 attribute commits to a certificate other than the one whose key verified the signature — its hash, or its issuer and serial, differ.
reasons.remedy: The signature is being presented under a different certificate for the same key. Supply the certificate the signer committed to; the attribute's hash identifies it.

reasons.returnedWhen: The timestamp response's status is neither granted nor grantedWithMods, so it carries no token. The message carries the status, the TSA's text and its failure codes.
reasons.remedy: Act on the failure codes: badAlg means the TSA does not accept that digest, unacceptedPolicy that it does not issue under the policy requested, and so on. Ask again, or ask another TSA.

reasons.returnedWhen: The token breaks a rule RFC 3161 sets for tokens specifically: more than one signer, a tsa name its signing certificate does not hold, or a message imprint whose digest algorithm pkinative does not compute. A token with no signing-certificate attribute is PKI_REASON_CMS_ATTRIBUTE_INVALID, the rule every signer is held to; content that is not a TSTInfo cannot be read as a token at all and is PKI_REASON_INPUT_MALFORMED.
reasons.remedy: The TSA is non-conforming or the token was altered. A token that breaks these rules is not evidence of a time, whatever its signature says.

reasons.returnedWhen: The token's messageImprint differs from the hash the caller expected — of the request, of the data, or of the signature value it is meant to timestamp.
reasons.remedy: The token stamps something else. For a signature timestamp, the imprint is the hash of the SignerInfo's signature value octets, without tag or length.

reasons.returnedWhen: The token does not answer the request that was sent: the request carried a nonce the token does not echo as the same integer, or asked for a policy the token was not issued under.
reasons.remedy: Do not retry the same response. A missing or different nonce is what a replayed or substituted response looks like; send a new request with a new nonce.

reasons.returnedWhen: A named PkiLimits bound stopped the search.
reasons.remedy: The limit field names it. Raise it only for input you trust; path building is exponential in the candidate set.
